competitors.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol) Developer Guide: Build, Deploy & Secure AI Tool Integrations in 2026
key_points: OWASP released 'A Practical Guide for Secure MCP Server Development' in February 2026
Input validation: never pass user input directly to shell commands, SQL queries, or filesystem ops
Least privilege: scoped API keys, read-only DB connections, restricted filesystem paths
Every tool invocation must require explicit user approval — never auto-approve destructive operations
Rate limiting prevents runaway AI loops generating thousands of API calls in seconds
For remote servers, always use HTTPS with TLS 1.3; for stdio, sandbox the subprocess
Audit logging every tool invocation with timestamps, parameters, and results

competitors.title: Complete Guide to MCP in 2026 — Architecture, Implementation, and Enterprise Roadmap
key_points: Production adoption checklist organized around security, governance, and monitoring phases
Auth/AuthZ: remote servers require OAuth 2.1 + PKCE; no hardcoded API keys — use Vault
Input validation: prompt injection defense, PII detection, minimum-privilege token scopes
Server evaluation: source code audit, version pinning, supply chain security verification
Rate limiting: per-user/agent request limits, cost tracking with per-request token logging
Observability: OpenTelemetry tracing, request/response logging, error rate dashboards
Health checks: MCP server availability monitoring, session state tracking, auto-recovery

competitors.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) 2026: Complete Integration & Security Guide
key_points: Parameterized queries prevent SQL injection in MCP database tools
Read-only operations (no DELETE, UPDATE exposed) as security boundary
Result limits prevent data exfiltration via unbounded queries
Rate limiting: max 100 requests/hour per client with request tracking
Input validation blocks SQL injection patterns, command injection, and dangerous characters
Length limits prevent resource exhaustion via large inputs

competitors.title: MCP Security Best Practices (Official Documentation)
key_points: Confused deputy problem: MCP proxy servers using static client IDs are vulnerable to authorization code theft
Per-client consent storage required: maintain registry of approved client_id values per user
Consent UI must clearly identify requesting MCP client, display scopes, show registered redirect_uri
OAuth state parameter validation is critical to prevent authorization code interception and CSRF
Token passthrough is explicitly forbidden — MCP servers must validate tokens were properly issued to them
Redirect URI validation must use exact string matching, not patterns or wildcards
